title: TASK#STOMP PowerShell Backdoor Steals Business Documents and Maintains Persistent Remote Access
content_md: Its decoded payloads search local drives, watch for new files, and send collected data to two command-and-control servers. The malware can also capture screenshots, steal saved Wi-Fi passwords and clipboard text, and execute commands from an operator. The observed chain begins when Windows Script Host runs a VBScript file from a user’s desktop. Researchers have not established how the file arrived, so its initial delivery method remains unknown. The script creates four scheduled tasks from XML files under LOCALAPPDATA and places msdiag.vbs in the user’s Startup folder. Together, these mechanisms can relaunch the malware after sign-in or a restart. TASK#STOMP Backdoor Steals Documents The installer stages files in a folder named WinDefendSvc , a name that resembles a Windows security component. It launches two hidden PowerShell scripts, sysloader.ps1 and winconn.ps1 , after terminating older instances. It also changes the modification times of five staged files to January 15, 2024, making them appear older than the observed activity. Each script reads a Base64-encoded DAT file, decodes its PowerShell payload, and executes it in memory. The primary payload, diagpack.dat , handles document collection and surveillance. Encoded VBS Script (Source: securonix) The secondary payload, winconncfg.dat , maintains a separate remote-access channel.
